ntp_servers.description: List of primary NTP servers for time synchronization. Prefer reliable, geographically close servers. Unset keeps the shipped commented line (example: ['0.pool.ntp.org', '1.pool.ntp.org', '2.pool.ntp.org', '3.pool.ntp.org']).

fallback_ntp_servers.description: Fallback NTP servers used when primary servers are unreachable. Must be a subset of or distinct from primary servers. Unset keeps the shipped commented line (example: ['0.pool.ntp.org', '1.pool.ntp.org']).

root_distance_max_sec.description: Maximum allowed root distance (round-trip delay to authoritative time source) in seconds. Servers exceeding this are rejected. Unset keeps the shipped commented line (example: 256).

poll_interval_min_sec.description: Minimum interval (in seconds) between successive polls to the same server. Lower values increase responsiveness but traffic. Unset keeps the shipped commented line (example: 32).

poll_interval_max_sec.description: Maximum interval (in seconds) between polls. Higher values reduce network usage but slow detection of clock drift. Unset keeps the shipped commented line (example: 2048).

max_steps_threshold_sec.description: Maximum clock offset (in seconds) that triggers a step instead of gradual slew. Offsets beyond this cause an immediate jump.

step_backward.description: Whether to allow stepping the clock backward (e.g., after network partition recovery). Set to `true` only if your services tolerate backward time jumps.

preserve_system_clock.description: If enabled, systemd will save and restore system time across reboots to reduce drift. Safe and recommended for most systems.

server_poll_interval_dampening.description: Poll interval growth factor during instability (e.g., 2 = exponential backoff). Higher values reduce oscillation but slow recovery.
